To All Residents of This Building

Illegal dumping, including leaving items on curbs, in parks or beside shared bins without permission, can result in a fine.
Never leave waste in hallways or next to a full bin; let the property manager know instead.
In apartments and condos, bulky items go to the building's own bulky item area; ask the property manager where it is.
Ask your property manager or building superintendent where the shared bins and the bulky item area are.

Sorting reminders:
- Do not guess with greasy baking cups: they belong in the green cart. Empty out leftover food into the green cart.

Regards,
Building Management

Which Bin Does It Go In?

In Tidewell we have three carts at home: blue for recycling, green for organics and black for garbage.

- Honey jars? They go into your blue recycling cart. Empty them out first.
- Cotton swabs belong in the black garbage bin.
- Glass kombucha bottles? They go in the blue recycling cart. Make sure they are completely empty.
- What about ceramic dishes? They are garbage and go in the black cart.
- Power tools? They belong at an electronics drop-off, never in a curbside cart. Take out any batteries first.

Great job, waste heroes!

Getting Rid of a Refrigerator

Refrigerators and freezers are bulky items. If you live in a house, book a bulky item pickup in advance through the waste service's website, app or customer service line. When you book, mention that the appliance contains refrigerant so it can be handled properly. Air conditioners and dehumidifiers also contain refrigerant, so mention it for those too.

For child safety, remove the doors or tape them shut before you set the fridge out. Put it at the curb the evening before the scheduled pickup day.

If you live in an apartment or condo, ask your property manager about the building's designated bulky item area.

If the fridge still works, consider donating it to a charity or reuse centre instead.

Collection schedule: what residents need to know

How do I know my pickup day?
Each area has its own collection day; the calendar for your area is on the website and in the app.

How frequently is the green bin emptied?
Green cart collection happens once a week.

Do garbage and recycling get picked up on the same week?
The blue recycling cart and the black garbage cart are collected on alternating weeks.

Can I put my bins out the night before?
Set carts out the evening before pickup or early that morning.

When do I have to bring my carts back in?
Take your carts back in by the end of collection day.

Is there pickup on public holidays?
If there is a public holiday in the week, pickup may happen one day later.

The Battery Who Wanted to Be Recycled

Once upon a time, a little battery lay at the bottom of a kitchen drawer. "I want to be recycled," said the battery. "Maybe I can ride in the blue cart!"

"No!" said a wise old cardboard box. "Batteries can spark and start fires in carts and trucks. You need to go somewhere special."

The family read the waste guide together. They put a piece of clear tape over the battery's ends so it could not spark. Then they drove it to the household hazardous waste drop-off, where trained staff took care of it.

"That was much safer," said the battery. And it was right. Batteries of every kind go to a hazardous waste drop-off, never in a cart.

Recycling Basics

The blue recycling cart is for clean paper, cardboard, rigid plastic containers, metal cans, foil, glass bottles and jars, and cartons.

The basics:
- Put caps and lids back on bottles, jugs and jars.
- Everything must be empty, clean and dry.
- Put recyclables in loose; never bag them.
- Flatten cardboard boxes so they fit with the lid closed.

Item by item:
- Soup cans: Empty them out first. Rinse out any residue.
- Toilet paper rolls: Place them loose in the cart, not in a bag.
- Just a reminder that soda cans belong in the blue recycling bin. Empty them out first. Give them a quick rinse.
- Fabric softener jugs: Empty them out first. Give them a quick rinse. Put the cap or lid back on.
- Empty spice jars: Empty them out first. Rinse out any residue. Screw the cap back on before recycling.
- If you have cereal boxes, they are accepted in the blue recycling cart. Remove the plastic liner and put the liner in the garbage. Flatten them.
- Moving boxes: Pour out anything left inside. Flatten them. Keep them clean and dry.
- Shampoo bottles? They are accepted in the blue recycling cart. Empty them out first. Rinse them out quickly. Good to know: Pumps contain metal springs, so remove pumps and put them in the garbage.

Remember: Rigid plastic packaging such as tubs and jugs belongs in recycling.

After the holidays, recycle plain wrapping paper and boxes, and put ribbons, bows and foil wrap in the garbage.

Organics (Green Cart)

Organics in Tidewell go in the green cart and are turned into compost.

General rules:
- Line the kitchen pail with newspaper or a paper bag if you want to.
- All food scraps are accepted, including meat, bones and dairy.
- No plastic of any kind, including bags labelled compostable.

Common items:
- Fish scraps: Take the food out of any packaging first.
- Have bread, pasta and rice to get rid of? They count as organics and go in the green cart. Unwrap them before they go in the cart. Leftovers, peels, bones and dairy all go in the green organics cart.
- Pumpkins: Strip off decorations before disposal.
- Dairy products: Remove any plastic packaging first.

In short: Paper with food or grease on it cannot be recycled, but it can be composted in the green cart.

Repair items when you can instead of replacing them.

Common Sorting Mistakes

Mistake: putting paper coffee filters in the blue recycling cart. Instead: Just a reminder that paper coffee filters belong in the green cart. That is because food and soiled paper are turned into compost.
Not in a hazardous waste drop-off: coconut water cartons. Correct: Residents often ask about coconut water cartons. They are accepted in the blue recycling cart. Make sure they are completely empty. Rinse them with a little water. Screw the cap back on before recycling. Drink and food cartons belong in the blue cart.
Not in the garbage: used muffin liners. Instead: And used muffin liners? They go in the green organics cart. Scrape out food scraps first. Paper that is soiled with food or grease goes in the green organics cart.
Not in the blue recycling cart: extinguishers. Do this: Extinguishers? They belong at a household hazardous waste drop-off, not in any cart.
Not in a hazardous waste drop-off: magazines. Instead: If you have magazines, they are recyclable in the blue cart. Keep them clean and dry. Never put them in a plastic bag first. Why? Because the blue cart is for clean paper, cardboard and empty containers.

Help line call summary

Assistant: Thanks for calling. What can I help with?
User: How should I prepare stuffed animals before throwing them out?
Assistant: Stuffed animals are accepted at textile drop-off bins. Consider donating them if they are in good shape. Wash and dry them, then put them in a tied bag. This is because textiles can be reused or turned into new fibres.
User: Also, What happens to cat litter? Which bin?
Assistant: In short, cat litter must go in the black garbage cart. Bag it and tie the bag closed. This is because there is no recycling market for it.
User: Great, thank you.
Assistant: Thanks for sorting carefully.

How to Sort Items Not on the List

You don't need to memorize every item. Look at what it is made of:
1. Take every type of battery to a household hazardous waste drop-off.
2. Drinking glasses, window glass, mirrors and ovenware are not recyclable; wrap them and put them in the garbage.
3. Empty and rinse cartons, put the cap back on, and recycle them. For example: coconut water cartons, protein shake cartons, juice boxes.
4. Textiles never go in the recycling cart; donate them or use a textile drop-off. Like: clothing.
5. Straws, plastic cutlery and loose caps are too small to recycle.
6. Plastic objects that are not containers, such as toys, hangers and toothbrushes, go in the garbage.

Sorting Directory

Empty prescription vials - blue cart. They must be empty before they go in the cart. Give them a quick rinse. Screw the cap back on before recycling. Only empty plastic vials go in recycling; leftover medications go to pharmacy take-back.
See also: empty pill bottles, empty medicine vials

Glass ovenware - garbage (black cart). Consider donating it if it is in good shape. Wrap sharp pieces in newspaper first.

Junk mail - blue recycling cart. Keep it clean and dry. Place it loose in the cart, not in a bag. Envelopes with plastic windows are accepted.
Includes: envelopes, mail, window envelopes

Paper bags - blue cart recycling. They must be empty before they go in the cart. Flatten them. Paper bags can also be reused to line your kitchen organics pail.
Also called: paper shopping bags, paper grocery bags

Plastic cutlery - the garbage.

Plastic takeout containers - blue cart recycling. Scrape them clean of food. Rinse out any residue. Foam takeout containers are not recyclable and go in the garbage.
Also called: plastic food containers, deli containers

Waste Guide: A to Z - selected items

Bread, pasta and rice - green cart. Take the food out of any packaging first.
Includes: stale bread, leftover pasta, cooked rice

Coconut water cartons - the blue bin. They must be empty before they go in the cart. Rinse them quickly. Screw the cap back on before recycling.

Disposable razors - the black bin. Wrap them well so no one gets cut. Cover the blade so collection workers are not cut.
Includes: razor blades, shaving razors

Dressers - bulky item pickup (book ahead). Book a pickup ahead of time; apartment residents should use the building's bulky item area. Consider donating them if they are in good shape.

Food cans - the blue bin. Tip out anything left inside. Rinse out any residue. Put the lid inside the can and pinch the top closed so the sharp edge is covered.

Margarine tubs - recycling (blue cart). Scrape out food scraps first. Rinse them with a little water. Leave the lid on.

Pool chemicals - hazardous waste drop-off. Keep them in the original, labelled container with the lid sealed. Keep them separate from other products.
Includes: chlorine tablets, pool chlorine

The Residential Waste Guidance team

Rule practice sheet

Do not guess from the product brand. Ask: what material is this, and which rule covers that material?

Material rule: Glass that is not a bottle or jar goes in the garbage.
Correct stream: the black bin.

Items that follow this rule:
- Broken window glass (non-container glass): Residents often ask about broken window glass. It must be placed in the garbage. Glass that is not a bottle or jar goes in the garbage.
- Baking dish lids (non-container glass): Got baking dish lids to get rid of? They should be placed in the garbage. Wrap them in newspaper or put them in a box labelled as broken glass. Drinking glasses, window glass, mirrors and ovenware are not recyclable; wrap them and put them in the garbage.
- Pottery (ceramic): material class → ceramic. Drinking glasses, window glass, mirrors and ovenware are not recyclable; wrap them and put them in the garbage. When it comes to pottery, it is collected with the garbage in the black cart.
- Mirrors (non-container glass): Do not guess with mirrors: they belong in the black garbage cart. Wrap sharp pieces in newspaper first. Non-container glass melts differently and cannot be recycled, so it goes in the garbage.

If a future item is made of the same material, use the same destination.

How to place an unfamiliar item

Residents often ask about items that are not in the A-Z list. Teach the material rule, then give examples.

Rule: If it is clean paper or cardboard, recycle it in the blue cart.
That material belongs in blue cart.

Items that follow this rule:
- Catalogs (paper): According to the guide, catalogs are collected in the blue recycling cart. Because: Paper and cardboard that are clean and dry belong in the blue cart.
- Holiday cards (paper): If you have holiday cards, they belong in the blue recycling cart. Make sure they are dry; wet paper is hard to recycle. If it is clean paper or cardboard, recycle it in the blue cart.
- Newspapers (paper): material class → paper. If it is clean paper or cardboard, recycle it in the blue cart. Newspapers? They belong in the blue cart.
- Cereal boxes (boxboard): Residents often ask about cereal boxes. They are part of your blue cart recycling. Because: Dry, clean paper and flattened cardboard go in recycling.
- Gift wrap (paper): material class → paper. If it is clean paper or cardboard, recycle it in the blue cart. If you have gift wrap, it goes into the blue recycling cart.

If a future item is made of the same material, use the same destination.

Rules, warnings and fines - our waste guide

What is contamination?
Contamination means putting the wrong items in a cart, such as plastic bags in recycling or plastic in organics.

My cart was tagged. What do I do now?
After a warning tag, remove the items that do not belong and try again on your next pickup day.

Are there fines for contamination?
Repeated contamination after warnings can lead to a fine.

Can I leave stuff beside the shared bins?
Illegal dumping is fined.

Why can't batteries go in the garbage?
Carts must never contain hazardous waste or batteries.

Residents' FAQ

Where are chip bags supposed to go?
The guide says chip bags go in the garbage.

How should I prepare game consoles before throwing them out?
For game consoles: they belong at an electronics drop-off, never in a curbside cart. Remove the batteries if you can and drop them off separately. Anything with a plug, cord or battery is electronic waste and goes to an electronics drop-off.

What happens to plastic buckets? Which bin?
Plastic buckets belong in the black garbage cart. Empty them out first.

How do I dispose of milk cartons?
Milk cartons belong in the blue cart, according to the waste guide. Empty them completely first. A quick rinse is enough; they do not need to be spotless. Leave the lid on.

What's the correct bin for cotton work gloves?
Cotton work gloves belong in textile donation, not the recycling cart. Usable ones can be donated. Bag them and keep them dry.

Is it okay to leave a mattress on the curb?
Putting bulky items at the curb without booking counts as illegal dumping.

Apartments and condos

I live in an apartment. Where does my garbage go?
If you live in an apartment, you share bins with your building.

Do apartment residents need to separate recycling?
Sorting rules are the same in apartments as in houses: recycling, organics and garbage are kept separate.

Who can tell me where my building's bins are?
Your property manager can show you where the shared bins and bulky item area are.

Can I leave garbage in the hallway?
Never leave waste in hallways or next to a full bin; let the property manager know instead.

How to Sort Items Not on the List

If an item is not in the A-Z guide, these rules will usually tell you where it goes:
1. Items too large to fit in a cart with the lid closed, including large appliances, are bulky items.
2. If it is clean paper or cardboard, recycle it in the blue cart. Examples: cereal boxes.
3. Rigid plastic containers such as bottles, jugs, tubs and clamshells go in the blue recycling cart once they are empty and rinsed. Think: plastic peanut butter jars, plastic takeout containers, empty prescription vials.
4. Check the label: warning symbols mean household hazardous waste. Think: fire extinguishers, paint thinner and solvents, mercury thermometers.
5. Plants, leaves and garden cuttings go in the green cart. For example: grass clippings, houseplants and cut flowers.
6. Leftovers, peels, bones and dairy all go in the green organics cart.
7. Medications and needles go back through a pharmacy take-back program. For example: needles and sharps, medications.

Rule: Dry, clean paper and flattened cardboard go in recycling.

Putting items in the wrong cart is called contamination. A warning tag means your cart had items that do not belong. Fix the problem the tag describes and set the cart out next time. 9. Plastic bags, wraps and wrappers go in the garbage because they tangle recycling machines. For example: candy wrappers, plastic wrap, plastic bags.

Hazardous Waste Basics

Household hazardous waste includes products that are flammable, corrosive, toxic or explosive, plus batteries and anything containing mercury.

The basics:
- Small household quantities are accepted free of charge.
- Keep products in their original, labelled containers with lids sealed.
- Never put hazardous waste in any curbside cart or pour it down a drain.
- Bring it to a community drop-off depot or a household hazardous waste collection event.

Item by item:

Hazardous Waste Basics

Hazardous products and batteries never go in a cart. They go to a community drop-off depot or a household hazardous waste collection event.

Key rules:
- Keep products in their original, labelled containers with lids sealed.
- Never put hazardous waste in any curbside cart or pour it down a drain.
- Bring it to a community drop-off depot or a household hazardous waste collection event.
- Small household quantities are accepted free of charge.

Items residents ask about:
- Lithium-ion batteries: Cover the terminals with clear tape.
- Do not guess with household cleaners: they count as household hazardous waste. Make sure the lid is sealed and the label is readable. Keep them separate from other products.
- Camera batteries: Put clear tape over the terminals to prevent sparks.
- If you have old thermometers, they have to be taken to a household hazardous waste drop-off. Why? Because they can harm workers and the environment.
- In Tidewell, camping fuel cylinders should be brought to a hazardous waste drop-off.
- Cordless tool packs: Tape the contact points first.
- Household batteries: Put clear tape over the terminals to prevent sparks.

In short: Dangerous household products must go to a hazardous waste drop-off, never in a cart or down the drain.
